project_footer_CTA: Ready to style your institution's digital presence? Let's create something fashionable together.
pageSummary:
Background
LIM College is a private institution in New York City focused on the business of fashion. In 2023 the college decided to refresh its public‐facing website. The existing site ran on Drupal 9 and contained an extensive body of program information, admissions and financial‑aid content, news stories and landing pages. To improve the user experience and modernize the brand without starting from scratch, LIM engaged Carnegie Higher Ed to develop the creative strategy and Knectar to implement the redesign. The guiding principle was to keep as much of the existing Drupal implementation and content intact as possible while applying an updated look and feel. This approach preserved the college's investment in content and infrastructure, kept the project within budget and minimized disruption for content editors.

Project objectives and creative strategy

Goals from Carnegie's assessment
During discovery sessions with LIM, Carnegie identified key problems with the legacy site: the navigation structure was confusing, program pages did not answer prospective students' questions and calls‑to‑action were buried. The creative strategy therefore set the following goals:

  • Refine information architecture and navigation. Carnegie recommended removing the "Online Learning" link from the primary navigation, creating dedicated pages for online programs and renaming Internships+ to Careers & Internships. They also advised clarifying the relationship between Admissions & Aid and Apply to LIM so that the former served as a high‑level overview and the latter focused on the application process.
  • Develop a dynamic homepage. Content models proposed by Carnegie stressed the need for an immersive homepage that introduces LIM's brand message, displays a program finder, showcases student success stories, highlights key statistics and promotes calls to action such as Request Info, Visit and Apply.
  • Create persuasive program pages and a program finder. Carnegie's wireframes defined separate templates for a program finder and academic program pages. The program finder allows users to search programs by degree level, modality (on‑campus or online), area of study and career field, then presents results in a streamlined list with calls to action. The program page content model includes a snapshot with a Request for Information (RFI) form, sections on what students will learn and career outcomes, faculty profiles, alumni/student spotlights, optional student work galleries and related programs.
  • Simplify enrollment messaging. The content priorities call for clear, intuitive instructions that streamline enrollment and help prospects progress through the funnel.
  • Support multilingual audiences. Analytics showed that non‑English sessions were a small but meaningful segment of site traffic and concentrated on admissions, academics and visit pages. Carnegie recommended piloting overview pages in Mandarin and Spanish that summarize admissions, cost, aid and program information.
  • Project‑to‑process mindset. Carnegie's plan envisioned the refresh as the beginning of an ongoing improvement cycle. Continuous enhancements—through usability testing, analytics‑informed refinements and incremental functionality—would help LIM keep its content relevant and extend the life of the site.

Design system and writing plan
The creative strategy updated LIM's design system and defined a writing plan. New or refreshed components included two‑ and three‑column callouts, faculty feeds, image and video carousels, stat panels, testimonial panels, a social‑media feed, an embedded RFI form and an NYC gallery. Carnegie identified which top‑level pages, new pages (e.g., Undergraduate Degrees, Graduate Degrees, Online Degrees) and program pages would be rewritten. Key project metrics were established for user experience, design, functionality and content—including increasing traffic to admissions and online program pages, improving mobile performance and site search, and rewriting program pages to emphasize career outcomes.

Implementation approach — Knectar

Leveraging existing infrastructure
Knectar was tasked with translating Carnegie's creative vision into a functional site without rebuilding the entire platform. Our technical assessment recommended applying the new design to the existing Drupal 9 implementation rather than building a completely new front‑end. The legacy front‑end already used a modern build pipeline with a style‑guide library; by keeping class names consistent and modifying styles, Carnegie's front‑end developers could update the look without altering markup. Only pages that were entirely redesigned—such as the homepage—required new markup and twig templates.

We also evaluated which content types needed modification. Most existing content types could be retained, but the homepage and degree (program) templates required significant restructuring, and the event content type (powered by a proprietary Zensource module) would need to be replaced. The new program pages and program finder would therefore become custom templates within Drupal. Given that the Zensource modules also provided the legacy events calendar and editing theme, we planned to rebuild those functions and replace the analytics dashboard with a standard solution such as Google Analytics.

Building new templates and components
Working closely with Carnegie's wireframes, Knectar built three primary templates:

  • Homepage template. We created a flexible Drupal content type for the homepage that integrates Carnegie's components: a hero banner for the brand message; a program finder block; a video testimonial gallery (Learn by Doing); an animated stats panel (Record that Speaks for Itself); an NYC photo gallery; an Instagram feed and a call‑to‑action panel. The template allows editors to assemble these sections using paragraph components, ensuring the page is dynamic yet easy to maintain.
  • Program finder. The program finder uses a custom Drupal view combined with filters for degree level, modality, area of study and career field, matching Carnegie's specifications. Results are loaded asynchronously for performance and present program titles, areas of study and career paths. Each result links to its program page and includes contextual calls to action such as Request Info and Apply.
  • Program page template. We replaced the legacy degree content type with a new program content type. Fields capture program snapshots, learning outcomes, career outcomes, faculty, alumni spotlights, student work galleries, featured courses and related programs. An embedded RFI form appears near the top, allowing visitors to request information without leaving the page. We migrated existing degree data into the new content type to maintain search‑engine rankings and continuity.

Updating the design system in Drupal
To support Carnegie's refreshed design system, Knectar implemented new and updated components as Drupal paragraph types. For example, two‑ and three‑column callouts, faculty feeds and image/video carousels were re‑implemented with accessible markup. The stat panel replaced the older accolade/stat slider component, which the component inventory had identified for replacement. Similarly, we removed the old Spotlight component and replaced tabbed interfaces with accordions to address accessibility issues. The new components use modern CSS and follow WCAG 2.1 guidelines for contrast and keyboard navigation.

Global elements such as the header, navigation and footer were re‑themed to match Carnegie's typography and color palette. Navigation labels were updated (e.g., Careers & Internships) and the application and request‑information links were emphasized, reflecting Carnegie's information‑architecture recommendations. A responsive navigation menu and optimized mobile layouts improved the mobile experience, addressing the high share of mobile sessions noted in the baseline analytics.

Integrations and accessibility
Because LIM's enrollment process relies on lead generation, integrating RFI forms was critical. The embedded RFI component submits data directly to the college's existing CRM, enabling admissions staff to follow up with prospects. We configured the forms to respect privacy regulations and provided clear consent messaging. Search‑engine optimization was improved by implementing semantic HTML, schema.org markup on program pages, and a more robust site search backed by Drupal's search API.

Accessibility compliance was a priority throughout the implementation. In addition to replacing tabbed components with accordions, we audited all templates against WCAG 2.1 Level AA standards. Images include meaningful alternative text, carousels provide play/pause controls and ARIA labels, and navigation can be used entirely with a keyboard. Color palettes were tested for contrast, and the site supports high‑contrast mode and screen‑reader landmarks.

Outcomes and impact
The redesigned LIM College website launched as a collaborative effort between Carnegie Higher Ed's strategic design and Knectar's technical implementation. Key achievements include:

  • Improved navigation and information architecture. The top‑level navigation now clearly differentiates academics, admissions, student life, careers & internships, and about sections, with dedicated pages for online and graduate programs.
  • Dynamic homepage and program finder. Prospective students can quickly explore programs through the homepage program finder and filter options by degree level, modality, area of study and career field.
  • Robust program pages. Each program page combines program overviews, career outcomes, faculty profiles and alumni stories, supported by embedded RFI forms. These pages help LIM articulate the value of its programs and encourage inquiries.
  • Updated design system. New components—stat panels, carousels, testimonial panels, call‑to‑action panels and social media feeds—deliver an engaging experience while keeping the underlying Drupal structure intact.
  • Accessibility and mobile performance. Replacing the old tab components with accordions, ensuring proper semantics and optimizing layouts for mobile devices have made the site more inclusive. Baseline analytics showed that 48 % of sessions occurred on mobile and that mobile visitors had shorter sessions; the new design directly addresses these issues.
  • Foundation for continuous improvement. By preserving the Drupal architecture and implementing Carnegie's process‑oriented strategy, the project sets the stage for ongoing enhancements. Editors can manage content with familiar paragraph and layout tools, and the site can evolve with additional components or A/B‑tested changes without a wholesale rebuild.

Acknowledgements
This case study highlights a successful collaboration between Carnegie Higher Ed and Knectar. Carnegie created the information‑architecture recommendations, content models, wireframes and writing plan that informed the redesign. Knectar implemented the project in Drupal 9, including new templates, a program finder, refreshed components, accessibility compliance and integrations. Together, these efforts produced a modern, user‑centered website that reflects LIM College's brand and supports its recruitment goals.
